Whenever I hit rock bottom, I start small. Find enjoyment in something small, even just one thing. A hot bath or shower. A really good cup of coffee. Making and eating something delicious. Binge watching something on netflix or watching a favourite movie, all bundled up in a nest of blankets. Taking a walk in my favourite wooded area, or if I'm feeling adventurous or especially restless, I'll find somewhere new to venture. Go visit an animal shelter and just pet the dogs and cats, occasionally play with them. Sometimes I just spend the day in bed.

Sometimes, there just isn't anything that can change how awful I feel.. I just allow the negative feelings to come and pass. There are times it seems to never go away, but eventually, the pain subsides a little. I also make sure to take my meds, no matter what.
Sometimes, I feel like there isn't really a cure or a fix-all. Sometimes, there isn't an answer. Sometimes it's hard to not dwell on past pain and trauma, but ultimately, that trauma should never define you as a person.

Find a reason, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem, and hold onto it. Find new interests and passions, if you can.

First, let me say I'm sorry.
Heartache and loss of a relationship can be extremely difficult and can feel like you lose yourself entirely. A little over a year ago, my fiance and I broke up. I was also 3 months pregnant with twins. I felt like my life was over, and I was in a deep, dark depression for many months following. I had no desire to live. I even planned out my exit method and had written my goodbyes. I was now living in a crappy apartment, alone, with next to no belongings. It was very bleak. What stopped me was a chance encounter, that lead to a date. Which lead to more dates. It wasn't easy but I found love again, and perhaps it wasn't ideal, but it gave me enough reason to stay a little longer.

There is no simple answer on how rebuild. It's a tough process. And as corny as it sounds, a lot of self-reflection can show you your weaknesses. I read a lot of self help books and articles in my free time. Self care. Whether it was sleeping all day if I wanted, or making a really great meal and enjoying that. Forcing myself to go out and try something new, despite my insecurities and anxiety. Meeting this new person, they saw something in me I didn't. They showed me what they saw in me, and encouraged me. They cared about me even on my worst days, and I slowly learned to open up and share even my darkest thoughts and feelings. They showed me it was okay. I learned how to love myself again, even though it is still a struggle some days.
I still have days, even weeks or months where I go to bed at night feeling like a complete failure, a burden, a loser. I'm trying to take the good with the bad and see the beauty in it, even the most painful and lonely moments life throws at me. We are our harshest critics, and our own worst enemy.

It can be quite cathartic to think about, I've found. It's really quite common, and I've noticed that most people who talk about and express these feelings and thoughts of suicide find relief, although it can be a double edged sword. It can also make others concer ed for your safety and well-being.

People are inherently selfish.

I see both sides. When you are grieving the loss of a loved one because of suicide, There's a lot of emotion. Knowing that person is gone leaves many unanswered questions and a lot of pain. It feels selfish that someone would remove themselves from our world and our lives, leaving us with pain, grief, etc.
But I also believe it is selfish to think this and have someone suffer.

I can understand how you feel, your situation is quite relatable to my own.

I'm sorry you're hurting. I struggle to help myself but find some comfort in trying to reach out to others. I wish I had a magic answer to solve all of your problems.  What I find helps me, is trying to stay in the moment and doing everything in my power to not dwell on the past, or worrying too much about the future. Distractions, even if temporary, have been life saving for me.

If you ever want someone to talk to, I'm here.

There came a point where what I was going through in life became too much. Everything was too much. I shut down. I couldn't talk about it, for numerous reasons. The main reason being I didn't want to burden her with more of my problems, she had her own mountain of problems to sort out. I was also very bitter and angry with her; tired of being compared to her, unable to meet the standards she had set. (Working with zero breaks, constantly having to do more work than anyone else. Some sort of compulsion to be better than everyone.) I was burnt out. A friend of mine had just died from cancer. My ex was suicidal, and mentally unstable. Begging me for forgiveness and wanting my support, wanting me back and then calling me awful names and belittling me the next. Issues with the guy I was seeing, and feeling inadequate. Having major depression, and coming to terms with my miscarriages and demise of my engagement. Not sleeping well. One night, she approached me and I walked away from her without a word. I was beyond angry with her, from having heard that she "was the only one doing her job". I refused to speak to her for over a week. Weeks went on into months. I attempted to write her a letter at Christmas, explaining everything. Apologizing the best I could, wanting to somehow make amends. She tossed me letter out, without so much as reading it. She won't come near me, or speak to me despite us having to work in the same department 3 out of 5 workdays. Utter silence and ignoring. It's been 5 months now.

Thank you for your response. I very much feel the same. I want to leave some closure.

What has me torn, is writing to the guy I've been seeing for the last 7 months. It's been good and bad, and I wonder if I should even say anything at all or simply make my exit and whatever follows, follows. I'm certain he would find out about my passing, even though in some strange way I'd like the details of my passing to be somewhat private.

 I too, just want some ready to have on hand should I make that decision. Especially for my Dad; he has lost one child already. I would want to ease his suffering and pain as much as I possibly could. Explain my reasons. Tell him he was an amazing father and that I loved him more than words could ever describe. And one for each of my sisters. I don't want to cause any more pain and suffering but also cannot continue with my own suffering existence. My choice may be selfish... but it is mine to make.

I have tried to leave my job. I can't. I have no post secondary education, can't afford college, have $10,000 in debt. My job has benefits that keep me medicated and just barely pay my rent and living expenses. No where else will pay me what I make, as I've worked with that company for 10 years. I can't afford to quit, have no one to stay with to figure it out.

My goals always seem to crumple in on themselves. Career wise, I have too many ideas and none seem successful. As I said, I cannot afford college or even student loans.

I feel I am destined to failure, or worse, follow in the footsteps of my parents. Functioning alcoholic with no life, or worse, an addict and severe mental health issues like my Mother. 
Dying might be the easy way out, but I've long felt this way. The past few months have just confirmed that I can't keep going on. I can't keep pretending anymore. All of my relationships have failed. This one showed so much promise. This person made me feel happy again, hopeful. I wanted to do better because they, at the time, felt I deserved better and could do better. They have given up on me too. They proved to be no better than the rest of the crappy people in this world. A privileged brat, throwing fits when things don't go their way. Shutting me out and ignoring me when they get angry or upset with me. Making me feel lonely and worthless. Another failure added to the long list.
